text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Bulgarian Central Electoral Commission is expected to announce today the final results of the parliamentary elections held on Saturday. @

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency (PA) approved the sale of 70 percent of state owned cement maker Devnya Ziment for $44.55 million to the Bulgarian-Spanish investment consortium Marvex with $4.45 million due to be paid by May 5, chairman of the PA supervisory board Yosif Iliev said.
-- Bulgaria's National Social Insurance Institute is expected to pay a 10,000 levs compensation to pensioners in May, bringing the minimum monthly pension to 24,000 levs. @

-- Bulgaria's private Creditbank said it had raised capital to 30 billion levs from 10 billion levs. Former Privatisation Agency executive director Vesselin Blagoev was appointed as an executive director of Creditbank.

-- Bulgaria's private St. Nikola International Orthodox Bank decided to raise capital to 32.2 billion levs from 2.2 billion levs through a new issue of voting shares, the bank's director Tzvetan Nachev said.

-- Bulgaria's Interior ministry is expected to propose to the new parliament an amendment to the penal code to make phone tapping and video recording legal means for collecting evidence in criminal court cases, a Interior ministry senior official said.
-- The Bulgarian state national carrier Balkan Airlines said it would start talks with Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank for the consolidation of the airline's foreign debt.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet is expected to raise central heating prices by 20 percent from May 1, Energy ministry officials said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
